outlook.statement: The Company is positioned to participate meaningfully in Bharat's next phase of industrial and infrastructure-led growth with expanded product portfolio, integrated manufacturing capabilities, and growing presence across value-added coated steel products.

Planned investment in a new 6-hi Reversible Cold Rolling Mill represents another important step in strengthening the manufacturing ecosystem by deepening backward integration and enhancing ability to produce specialised cold-rolled steel in-house.
As manufacturing capacities commissioned during the year achieve higher levels of utilisation, they are expected to strengthen operational efficiency, product mix, and profitability.
Company expects consolidated revenues of Rs 1,500 Crore in FY 2026-27, supported by domestic coated-steel business and Nigerian subsidiary.
Following commissioning of new rolling mill from December 2027, Company expects revenues of approximately Rs 3,000 Crore in FY 2028-29.
Shift toward domestic raw material sourcing expected to deliver enhanced working capital efficiency, compressing cash conversion cycle.

Manufacturing outlook for FY 2026-27 remains positive as Manaksia Steels enters next phase of capacity expansion journey, focusing on maximising utilisation of Galvalume line, commissioning new 90,000 TPA colour coating line, and implementing Board-approved 6-hi Reversible Cold Rolling Mill project.
Company expects operating leverage to strengthen as recently commissioned capacities approach optimum utilisation, enabling incremental production to contribute disproportionately to profitability.
Will continue strengthening innovation capabilities through continuous process improvement, technology adoption and product development to address evolving customer requirements.

During FY 2026-27, will strengthen organisational capability to support commissioning of new Colour Coating line and increasing scale of operations through selective recruitment and capability enhancement.

Marketing priorities for FY 2026-27 will focus on expanding market reach, deepening customer engagement and strengthening presence across existing and new geographies. A key priority will be to broaden the portfolio of value-added products, including differentiated and premium offerings designed to address evolving customer preferences and niche market opportunities.

The commissioning of the new Colour Coating line and the planned Cold Rolling Mill will further strengthen the Company's ability to respond to changing market requirements with greater product flexibility, improved availability and enhanced manufacturing capability. These investments are expected to support faster market development while creating opportunities to serve a wider range of applications and customer segments.

ESG priorities for FY 2026-27: Environment - Increase renewable energy utilisation, strengthen energy-efficient technologies, enhance pollution control systems, improve water treatment and recycling, optimise resource consumption and continue green belt development. Social - Support capacity expansion through selective recruitment, employee learning and development, welfare initiatives, a collaborative and safe workplace, and greater use of digital HR systems. Governance - Strengthen risk management, regulatory compliance, ethical business conduct, transparency, stakeholder engagement, internal controls and operational monitoring.

CSR priorities for FY 2026-27: Education - Expand support to a larger number of underprivileged children and strengthen educational infrastructure in government schools. Community infrastructure - Continue developing and maintaining community assets that improve public welfare, dignity and environmental sustainability. Environmental sustainability - Expand initiatives relating to environmental conservation, resource efficiency, waste management and sustainable development. Women's empowerment - Explore additional opportunities for skill development and economic empowerment.

Growth will be shaped by a combination of strong domestic demand and resilient private consumption, supported by low inflation and GST rationalisation, alongside stable export performance with improved access to key markets. This momentum is further reinforced by sustained policy support, ongoing economic reforms, and a favourable demographic advantage.
Over the medium term, sustained consumption, gradual investment recovery, and expanding global trade linkages are expected to reinforce India's position as a key driver of global economic growth.

The World Bank has revised its FY 2026-27 growth estimate upward to approximately 6.6%, reflecting resilient domestic momentum even as growth moderates from the previous year. India is expected to retain its position as the fastest-growing major economy.

Security price risk: 10% change in prices of equity/mutual fund investments (FVTPL) would impact profit before tax by Rs 685.96 lacs (2025) and Rs 1048.67 lacs (2024); 10% change in equity instruments (FVOCI) would impact OCI before tax by Rs 170.16 lacs (2025) and Rs 233.80 lacs (2024).
